      What Is X?

      X is the rebranded version of Twitter — a social media platform where users post short messages (“posts”), interact with others, and access features like verified badges, premium subscriptions, and integrated AI tools Trusted Reviews+1.

      Origins and Rebrand

      X was formerly known as Twitter, the microblogging service launched in 2006. In October 2022, Elon Musk acquired Twitter for $44 billion and, after a series of changes, rebranded it to X in 2023 Trusted Reviews+1. The rebrand replaced the blue bird logo with a minimalist “X” icon and shifted the platform’s identity toward Musk’s vision of an “everything app” — a hub for text, video, audio, and even peer‑to‑peer finance Tech Review Advisor.

      Core Features

      • Posts: Users share short text messages (up to 280 characters for free accounts) and can also post images, videos (up to 140 seconds for free users), and longer-form content via paid tiers Trusted Reviews+2.

      • Interaction: Like, reply, quote, repost, and send direct messages Built In+1.

      • Follows: Users can follow others to see their posts in their feed; posts can be discovered via trending topics and hashtags Beebom.

      • Verification: The blue checkmark is now purchasable (from about $8/month) and tied to premium subscriptions, not just identity verification Trusted Reviews.

      • Premium Tiers:

        • X Premium: Ad‑free experience, larger post limits (up to 25,000 characters), access to Grok AI, boosted replies, and analytics Trusted Reviews+1.

        • Premium Business: Gold tick for organizations, ad credit, analytics, and priority support Trusted Reviews.

      Differences from Twitter

      • Verification: Now paid rather than free Trusted Reviews.

      • Content Limits: Daily post length cap of 2,400 characters; follow limit of 400 accounts; 500 daily DMs Trusted Reviews.

      • Monetization: Creators can earn from ad revenue sharing and premium features Tech Review Advisor.

      • AI Integration: Grok AI chatbot access for premium users Trusted Reviews+1.

      How People Use X

      X is used for news, political discussion, trends, community building, and marketing. It remains a major platform for journalists, politicians, celebrities, and everyday users Trusted Reviews+1.

      In short: X is Twitter’s successor — a social media app with the same core idea of short posts and public conversation, but with new monetization, AI features, and a broader “everything app” vision under Elon Musk’s leadership Trusted Reviews+2.
